newsitem.title: USA: Orange County bankruptcy trial to get underway.
newsitem.headline: Orange County bankruptcy trial to get underway.

text.p: Orange County, Calif., prosecutors will begin presenting their case on Monday in the trial of former assistant county treasurer Matthew Raabe on charges stemming from the county's financial crisis.
Opening statements are scheduled for early Monday in a Santa Ana courtroom. A 12-person jury, composed of six men and six women, was selected earlier this month for the trial.
The Raabe trial could last until mid-May, Deputy Orange County District Attorney Matthew Anderson said.
The county filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.

Raabe was indicted in May 1995 on several counts, including making false statements in the sale of securities and misappropriation of public funds. Raabe, who has denied any wrongdoing, faces up to 12 years in state prison.
Raabe was one of several Orange County officials to face charges following the bankruptcy.
In April 1995, former county treasurer Robert Citron pleaded guilty to six felonies for his role in the crisis.
A judge last November ordered him to spend a year in jail and pay a $100,000 fine, but Citron was later assigned to a community work program instead of jail.
Last October, a judge sentenced former Orange County budget director Ronald Rubino to probation for charges stemming from the investment crisis.
The case against county auditor Steven Lewis was put on hold by a state court pending a decision on his motion to disqualify the district attorney.
